name: B10-0235/2024 (ECR) – 11th year of the occupation of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol by the Russian Federation and the deteriorating human rights situation in occupied Crimea, notably the cases of Iryna Danylovych, Tofik Abdul
title: JOINT MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the 11th year of the occupation of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol by the Russian Federation and the deteriorating human rights situation in occupied Crimea, notably the cases of Iryna Danylovych, Tofik Abdulhaziiev and Amet Suleymanov
part_text:
The European Parliament condemns Russia's occupation of Crimea and calls for the release of three detained people: Iryna Danylovych, Tofik Abdulhaziiev and Amet Suleymanov. It says Russia has violated the rights of Crimean Tatars and other residents through detentions, forced conscription, censorship and pressure to assimilate. The Parliament asks the European Union to support programmes protecting Crimean Tatar culture and language. This is a statement of the Parliament's position; it does not change any law.

- The Parliament demands the release of the three named prisoners and all political prisoners in Crimea.
- It calls for medical care for them and for those responsible for their detention to be held to account.
- It asks the European Union to fund cultural, educational and media programmes for Crimean Tatars.
